title: Projective short exact sequences at every adic quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $K,E,M$ be $R$-modules, and $u:K\to E$, $v:E\to M$ be $R$-linear maps with $u$ injective, $v$ surjective and $\operatorname{im}(u)=\ker(v)$. Suppose $M$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $M/IM$ is projective over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For an $R$-module $L$ and $n\ge1$, let $I^nL$ be the submodule generated by $rx$ with $r\in I^n$ and $x\in L$, put $A_n=R/I^n$ and $L_n=L/I^nL$, and give $L_n$ its natural $A_n$-module structure. Write $q_n^L:L_{n+1}\to L_n$ for reduction. Then for every $n\ge1$, the induced $A_n$-linear maps $u_n:K_n\to E_n$, $[k]\mapsto[u(k)]$, and $v_n:E_n\to M_n$, $[e]\mapsto[v(e)]$, satisfy: $u_n$ is injective, $v_n$ is surjective, $\operatorname{im}(u_n)=\ker(v_n)$, and $M_n$ is projective over $A_n$. Moreover $q_n^Eu_{n+1}=u_nq_n^K$ and $q_n^Mv_{n+1}=v_nq_n^E$ for every $n\ge1$, as identities of $R$-linear maps.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$. Any $R$-linear map $f:L\to L'$ sends a generator $rx$ of $I^nL$ to $rf(x)\in I^nL'$, hence descends to $f_n:L_n\to L'_n$. Additivity and $f_n(\bar r\,[x])=[rf(x)]=\bar r f_n([x])$ show $A_n$-linearity. Also $I^{n+1}L\subseteq I^nL$, so the reduction maps are well-defined. Apply this to $u,v$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, proof: formation of the quotient sequences.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to K\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}M\to0$ and $N=A_n$. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed injectivity, surjectivity, image-kernel equality and flatness of $M$; it gives a short exact tensor sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring](1), identify $A_n\otimes_R L$ with $L_n$ via $\bar r\otimes x\mapsto[rx]$, for $L=K,E,M$. This identification is $A_n$-linear: multiplication by $\bar a$ sends both sides to $[arx]$. On a generator $1\otimes k$, the first tensor map becomes $[k]\mapsto[u(k)]$; likewise $1\otimes e$ gives $[e]\mapsto[v(e)]$. Thus the resulting maps are exactly $u_n,v_n$, proving all three exactness assertions.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, first proof sentence; Tag 00HL, lemma-flat-tor-zero; quotient identification as in Tag 051C.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] for $R\to A_n$, $A_n\otimes_RM$ is flat over $A_n$, hence so is $M_n$ under the $A_n$-linear identification of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring](1). Let $J_n$ be the image of $I$ in $A_n$. Products of $n$ elements of $J_n$ vanish, so $J_n^n=0$. The maps $A_n/J_n\to R/I$, $[[r]]\mapsto[r]$, and $M_n/J_nM_n\to M/IM$, $[[m]]\mapsto[m]$, are isomorphisms: their inverse formulas are the same, since $I^n\subseteq I$ and $J_nM_n=IM/I^nM$. They preserve scalar multiplication on representatives. Therefore the latter reduction is projective over $A_n/J_n$ by the hypothesis on $M/IM$. Apply [lem-trf-local-nilpotent-projective-flat-lift] over $A_n$ with ideal $J_n$ and module $M_n$ to obtain projectivity of $M_n$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, invocation of Tag 05CG, lemma-lift-projective; Tag 00HI, lemma-flat-base-change.

proof.text: For $k\in K$, both $q_n^Eu_{n+1}$ and $u_nq_n^K$ send $[k]_{n+1}$ to $[u(k)]_n$. For $e\in E$, both $q_n^Mv_{n+1}$ and $v_nq_n^E$ send $[e]_{n+1}$ to $[v(e)]_n$. Every quotient class has a representative, giving the two identities as $R$-linear maps for every $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, quotient sequences regarded as an inverse system; representative calculation.

lean.statement: theorem adic_quotient_projective_short_exact {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) {K : Type vK} [AddCommGroup K] [Module R K] {E : Type vE} [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] {M : Type vM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (u : K →ₗ[R] E) (v : E →ₗ[R] M) (hu : Function.Injective u) (hv : Function.Surjective v) (hex : Function.Exact u v) [Module.Flat R M] [Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))] : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Function.Injective (u.reduceModIdeal (I ^ n)) ∧ Function.Surjective (v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ n)) ∧ Function.Exact (u.reduceModIdeal (I ^ n)) (v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ n)) ∧ Module.Projective (R ⧸ I ^ n) (M ⧸ (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) ∧ (Submodule.factorPowSucc I E n).comp ((u.reduceModIdeal (I ^ (n + 1))).restrictScalars R) = ((u.reduceModIdeal (I ^ n)).restrictScalars R).comp (Submodule.factorPowSucc I K n) ∧ (Submodule.factorPowSucc I M n).comp ((v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ (n + 1))).restrictScalars R) = ((v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ n)).restrictScalars R).comp (Submodule.factorPowSucc I E n)
